Name: Little Orchard Farm (Content Patcher)
Author: yuninocorn
Description:
[b][size=5]General[/size][/b]
This content pack utilizes Pathoschild's Content Patcher to add a new farm type - the Little Orchard Farm. 

The starting farmhouse interior is decorated to match the intended overall feeling of the farm map - rustic, cozy, compact. You start with the usual 15 parsnip seeds. 
The farm itself offers just enough space to fit all of your farm buildings - including the magical ones, of course - without leaving too much open space.

Located in the top left corner of the map is its main feature - the orchard. It is originally blocked by stumps and boulders. There are 1-2 fully grown fruit trees of each type, except for banana and mango. 

There's a little river island in the bottom left corner that currently doesn't serve any special purpose, other than being a cozy fishing spot. The river holds fishes from the forest and town, as well as regular trash and algae. 

A decorated farm example is shown in the image tab of this mod page (this was built quickly, mainly to show the size and capacity of the farm layout. I'm sure there are ways to optimize the space better). 

[b][size=5]Good to know [/size][/b]
Sometimes when changing seasons, there may be a yellow 'skipped reload [...]' error message in your SMAPI console about loading the worldmap texture. This has no actual effect in the game and won't impact you while playing. It's just due to the way the mod loads its assets. 

[b][size=5]Installing [/size][/b]
To install this content pack, download the mod file and extract the .zip file to the 'Mods' folder in your Stardew Valley game folder. 

[b][size=5]Configurations[/size][/b]
Generic Mod Config Menu - If you are using Stardew Valley Expanded, you can check 'SVEWorldmapFix' to fix the hills on the left side of the map clipping into the mountain texture added by SVE. 

[size=5][b]Compatibility[/b][/size]
Unfortunately, the mod doesn't seem to work on mobile yet. 
I haven't used any custom tilesheets to construct this map, so recolor mods should generally work fine, as long as they do not drastically alter the terrain shapes. 

Feedback, questions and suggestions are always welcome. 

Enjoy!
